reforms.description: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOA) was enacted to address corporate governance issues and restore investor confidence following major accounting scandals. It established the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) and introduced new disclosure requirements and penalties for securities fraud.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reform aims to restore investor confidence, which can lead to increased investment and innovation in the economy.
reforms.status_evidence: The act was enacted and is currently in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act represents a significant overhaul of corporate governance and accountability standards.
reforms.source_quote: Congress passed the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOA), which took effect 30 July 2002. This is arguably the most important securities legislation since the 1930s.

reforms.description: The Telecommunications Act of 1996 aimed to spur local service competition by allowing Bell operating companies to enter long-distance service if local service was open to competition, linking the two goals to improve services and spur innovation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By promoting competition in telecommunications, the reform is expected to enhance service quality and foster innovation in the sector.
reforms.status_evidence: The act was enacted and is currently in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: The act represents a major reform in telecommunications policy, fundamentally changing the competitive landscape.
reforms.source_quote: The Telecommunications Act of 1996 began the national effort to spur local service competition.
